Yichun (Heilongjiang)|China.f: Nicknamed Lindu, the forest capital, this city in Heilongjiang has a greening rate of up to 83 percent.

Tonghua|China.f: In August 1945 Tonghua briefly served as the temporary capital of Manchukuo, where Puyi announced his abdication.

Huaihua|China.f: Huaihua is the heart of Dong country, home to nearly 28 percent of all the Dong people in China.

Hechi|China.f: Hechi moved its city seat in 2016 from Jinchengjiang, where it had been since 1953, to Yizhou District.

Mangshi|China.f: Dehong prefecture's TV station, in the Mangshi area, is the only one in China that broadcasts in four languages.

Liping|China.f: On 18 December 1934 the Communist Party Politburo met in Liping during the Long March and backed Mao's plan.

Altay|China.f: Dundbulag rock carvings near Altay city are among the very early evidence of skiing.

Mohe|China.f: Mohe, China's northernmost city, recorded -53.0 C on 22 January 2023, the lowest temperature ever measured in China.

Enshi|China.f: The oldest records of Enshi date to 776 BC, when the area was a state called Bazi that lasted until 476 BC.

Chaoyang|China.f: Known as China's fossil city, Chaoyang has yielded Early Cretaceous birds named after it, such as Sapeornis chaoyangensis.

Quzhou|China.f: Six B-25 bombers from the 1942 Doolittle Raid ran out of fuel and crash landed near Quzhou, including Doolittle's own.

Chifeng|China.f: Chifeng means red peak, taken from Hongshan, the Red Hill that also names the Neolithic Hongshan Culture.

Leshan|China.f: Forbidden City artifacts were stored in Leshan from July 1939 until the last batch left in March 1947.

Zhaotong|China.f: The Yi people consider Zhaotong their homeland, which they call Zizipuwu.

Garzê|China.f: Garze County in Kham climbs from 3,325 m at its lowest point to 5,688 m at its highest.

Qilian|China.f: Qilian Deer Farm, about 3,500 m up in the Qilian Mountains, is described as Asia's largest semi-wild deer breeding base.

Yutian|China.f: Yutian County was at the epicenter of a magnitude 7.1 earthquake on 21 March 2008.

Zhaosu|China.f: Zhaosu is famed as the land of heavenly horses for a horse-breeding history that stretches back centuries.

Nanyang|China.f: Nanyang produced four so-called sages: Zhang Heng of science, Zhang Zhongjing of medicine, Fan Li of commerce and Zhuge Liang.

Jiujiang|China.f: The poet Tao Yuanming, author of Peach Blossom Spring, lived at the foot of Mount Lu near Jiujiang.

Aral|China.f: Aral means island in Uyghur, and the city is headquarters of the 1st Division of the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps.

Tangshan|China.f: Tangshan is the birthplace of China's first standard-gauge railway, first steam locomotive and first cement factory.

Tumxuk|China.f: Tumxuk is a well known archaeological site for Serindian art, with Buddhist sculpture from the 5th to 7th centuries.

Changzhi|China.f: Changzhi means long rule, and in 1945 it hosted the Shangdang Campaign, the first KMT versus PLA battle after World War II.

Xinzhou|China.f: Xinzhou contains Mount Wutai, one of the four sacred mountains of Chinese Buddhism.

Hengyang|China.f: The Battle of Hengyang was the longest defense of a single city in the Second Sino-Japanese War.

Xiangxi|China.f: About two thirds of Xiangxi prefecture's people belong to 25 ethnic minorities, including 860,000 Tujia and 790,000 Miao.

Anyang|China.f: Anyang, known anciently as Yin, was the first stable capital in Chinese history, home to the Shang dynasty from the 14th century BC.

Ankang|China.f: Ankang County was established in AD 280 under the Western Jin, originally known as Xicheng.

Ganzhou|China.f: Ganzhou is home to the Harmony Clock Tower, described as the world's largest mechanical clock.

Wushan|China.f: Wushan's county seat sits at the western entrance to Wu Gorge, and the nearby Little Three Gorges on the Daning River are famous.

Kuqa|China.f: Kuqa, ancient Kucha, was home to the monk Kumarajiva, whose translations made hundreds of Buddhist texts available in Chinese.

Karamay|China.f: Karamay means black oil in Uyghur, and one of China's largest oil fields was discovered there in 1955.

Daqing|China.f: Daqing means Great Celebration, for the tenth anniversary of the PRC, and oil was discovered there in 1959.

Pu'er|China.f: Pu'er tea is named after Pu'er, and the city itself was formerly known as Simao.

Chizhou|China.f: Chizhou is home to Mount Jiuhua, one of the four sacred mountains of Chinese Buddhism.

Alxa Right Banner|China.f: Alxa Right Banner covers 71,515 square km yet had only about 22,600 residents in the 2020 census.

Meizhou|China.f: Seng Saekhu, from Meizhou, was the patriarch of Thailand's Shinawatra family and great-grandfather of Thaksin and Yingluck.

Wenshan|China.f: Wenshan is a producer of sanchi, a medicinal plant grown out of daylight under huge plastic sheets.

Nanchong|China.f: Emperor Gaozu of Han set up Anhan County here in 202 BC, and it became Nanchong in AD 742.
